title: From Process Learning to Production Control: Characterization for the Era of Heterogeneous Systems - Semiwiki
gist: SemiWiki recaps a PDF Solutions conference talk arguing that as chip innovation shifts from optimizing single dies to optimizing heterogeneous systems (chiplets plus advanced packaging), characterization must evolve from a process-learning tool into a continuous 'production intelligence' layer that connects manufacturing data across foundries, OSATs, and test stages.

insights.claim: Characterization's role in semiconductor manufacturing is evolving from enabling process learning (understanding transistor behavior, process variation, yield) to becoming the foundation for real-time production control of entire heterogeneous systems.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Signals a redefinition of what characterization tools/vendors need to deliver — from qualification data to live production-control feedback loops.
insights.quote: Its role is no longer limited to enabling process learning; it is becoming the foundation for production control.

insights.claim: The framework was presented by Ramune Nagisetty, Enterprise Account Director at PDF Solutions, at the IMAPS CHIPcon 2026 conference, positioning PDF Solutions as advancing a system-level characterization thesis to industry peers.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Identifies the primary source event; useful for tracking PDF Solutions' public messaging and competitive positioning in yield/test analytics.
insights.locator: Ramune Nagisetty, Enterprise Account Director at PDF Solutions, explored this evolution during a presentation at the IMAPS CHIPcon 2026 conference.

insights.claim: Dennard scaling (the voltage/power reduction that accompanied dimensional transistor scaling) slowed and effectively ended in the early 2000s, forcing PPA (performance, power, area) gains to come instead from material innovations like strained silicon, high-k metal gate, and new transistor architectures such as FinFET and Gate-All-Around.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Explains why the industry's PPA roadmap increasingly depends on packaging/system-level innovation rather than transistor scaling alone.
insights.quote: However, traditional Dennard scaling slowed and ended in the early 2000s.

insights.claim: Design Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO) optimizes PPA at the standard-cell/IP-block level, while the newer System Technology Co-Optimization (STCO) extends optimization beyond a single die by combining multiple specialized chiplets into an advanced package.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: STCO marks the industry's optimization unit moving from die to package/system — a lens for evaluating EDA and packaging vendors' roadmaps.
insights.locator: In parallel, design technology co-optimization (DTCO) has evolved as a method to improve PPA

insights.claim: Advanced packaging is no longer just the final manufacturing step; it now directly shapes power delivery, thermal performance, bandwidth, reliability, and overall system architecture, blurring the traditional line between front-end silicon and back-end packaging.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Reinforces the investment case for advanced-packaging equipment and materials suppliers as architecture decisions move earlier into the packaging domain.
insights.quote: Packaging is no longer simply the final manufacturing step.
insights.locator: Packaging Has Become Foundational to Architecture and Design

insights.claim: Heterogeneous systems now combine dies from multiple foundries, process nodes, and suppliers that only converge during advanced packaging, replacing the traditional single linear manufacturing flow with sequential assembly, package test, burn-in, final test, and system validation stages.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Multi-source chiplet supply chains increase coordination and traceability burden across foundries and OSATs — a structural cost/complexity driver to watch in chiplet-based product economics.

insights.claim: Every additional chiplet increases interfaces, failure mechanisms, test insertions, and manufacturing decisions, so overall manufacturing complexity grows faster than raw die count, while manufacturing knowledge simultaneously fragments across foundries, OSATs, and test operations.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Implies chiplet-based designs face superlinear test/yield-management cost scaling, favoring vendors that can unify cross-party manufacturing data.
insights.quote: Every additional chiplet increases interfaces, failure mechanisms, test insertions, and manufacturing decisions.
insights.locator: Complexity Grows Faster Than Die Count

themes.theme: New failure mechanisms in advanced packaging

insights.claim: Advanced packaging introduces failure and interaction mechanisms — mechanical stress, thermal coupling, through-silicon vias, hybrid bonding, package materials, and cross-layer effects — that conventional silicon-only characterization cannot fully capture.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Points to demand for new metrology/characterization techniques targeting package-level stress, thermal, and interconnect effects, not just transistor-level measurement.
insights.quote: Mechanical stress, thermal coupling, through-silicon vias, hybrid bonding, package materials, and cross-layer effects all influence system performance and reliability.
insights.locator: New Failure Mechanisms Require New Measurements

insights.claim: Short-flow characterization alone is no longer sufficient for heterogeneous systems; it must be complemented by full-flow test vehicles that capture interactions introduced during wafer thinning, die singulation, package assembly, and final integration.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Suggests test-vehicle and full-flow characterization spending will rise as a distinct budget line for chiplet/advanced-packaging programs.
insights.locator: Characterization Must Follow the Manufacturing Flow

insights.claim: Manufacturing knowledge generated at each stage (wafer fab, wafer sort, assembly, package test, burn-in, system validation) rarely travels between organizations, forcing downstream teams at different foundries, OSATs, and test facilities to rediscover what upstream processes already learned.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Identifies a concrete inefficiency (duplicated discovery cost) in fragmented multi-party chiplet supply chains that data-continuity/traceability platforms aim to monetize.
insights.quote: The industry has a data and knowledge continuity challenge.

insights.claim: PDF Solutions positions connected data, unit-level traceability, and feed-forward analytics — via its Data Feed Forward (DFF) architecture — as the mechanism to convert characterization into 'production intelligence,' enabling adaptive testing, improved yield prediction, earlier defect detection, and more accurate performance binning.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Names PDF Solutions' specific product architecture (DFF) as its answer to the fragmentation problem, relevant when benchmarking it against other yield-management/test-analytics vendors.
insights.quote: Rather than treating each manufacturing stage as an isolated checkpoint, production becomes a continuous learning system.
insights.locator: Connecting Knowledge Across the Manufacturing Flow

insights.claim: The article predicts that future competitive advantage in heterogeneous integration will not come from building better chiplets or more advanced packages alone, but from the ability to preserve, connect, and operationalize manufacturing knowledge across the entire production flow.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Frames data/knowledge integration capability, not raw process technology, as the durable moat to watch for in semiconductor manufacturing and OSAT competitiveness.
insights.quote: The leaders in heterogeneous integration will not simply build better chiplets or more advanced packages. They will be the companies that best preserve, connect, and operationalize manufacturing knowledge across the entire production flow.
